source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י אִם־יַעֲמֹ֨ד מֹשֶׁ֤ה וּשְׁמוּאֵל֙ לְפָנַ֔י אֵ֥ין נַפְשִׁ֖י אֶל־הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה שַׁלַּ֥ח מֵֽעַל־פָּנַ֖י וְיֵצֵֽאוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to me: If stood Moses and Samuel before me, not my soul [would be] toward the people the this; send [them] from before my face, and let them go out.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Though Moses and Samuel were to stand before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} soul [would] not [be] toward this people. Send [them] away from before {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face, and let them go out.
en.B: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Even if Moses and Samuel stood before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to plead for them, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart would not go out to this people. Send them away from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} presence; let them leave!
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Even if Moses and Samuel stood in front of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and prayed for these people, I would not be willing to help them. Send them away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Let them go!

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dijo: «Aunque Moisés y Samuel se pusieran delante de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} alma no [estaría] con este pueblo. Échalos de delante de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} rostro, y que salgan.
es.B: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dijo: «Aunque Moisés y Samuel se presentaran delante de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} para interceder por ellos, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} corazón no se inclinaría hacia este pueblo. Échalos de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} presencia; ¡que se vayan!
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me dijo: «Aunque Moisés y Samuel estuvieran delante de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} orando por esta gente, yo no estaría dispuesto a ayudarlos. Échalos de delante de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. ¡Que se vayan!

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me dit : « Quand Moïse et Samuel se tiendraient devant {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} âme ne [serait] pas tournée vers ce peuple. Renvoie-[les] de devant {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} face, et qu’ils s’en aillent.
fr.B: Puis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me dit : « Même si Moïse et Samuel se tenaient devant {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} pour intercéder pour eux, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} cœur ne se tournerait pas vers ce peuple. Chasse-les loin de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} présence ; qu’ils s’en aillent !
fr.R: Puis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} m’a dit : « Même si Moïse et Samuel se tenaient devant {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} et priaient pour ce peuple, je ne voudrais pas l’aider. Renvoie ces gens loin de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Qu’ils s’en aillent !

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaniambia, "Hata kama Musa na Samweli wangesimama mbele {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, nafsi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} isingekuwa kwa watu hawa. Waondoe mbele ya uso {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, waende zao.
sw.B: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaniambia, "Hata kama Musa na Samweli wangesimama mbele {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kuwaombea, moyo {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} usingewaelekea watu hawa. Waondoe mbele {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}; na waondoke!
sw.R: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaniambia, "Hata kama Musa na Samweli wangesimama mbele {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na kuwaombea watu hawa, nisingekubali kuwasaidia. Waondoe mbele {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. Waache waende!

decisions.choice: Moses and Samuel: the great intercessors of Israel's past
decisions.reason: Moses pleaded for the people after the golden calf and in the wilderness, and God held back his judgment (Exodus 32:11-14, 30-32; Numbers 14:13-20). Samuel prayed for Israel and promised never to stop praying for them (1 Samuel 7:5-9; 12:19-23). Psalm 99:6 names the two together as those who called on the LORD and were answered. Even prayers like theirs would not change the LORD's decision now.

decisions.choice: stand before me: stand in God's presence to plead for the people
decisions.reason: To stand before the LORD is to serve him; here it means standing before him as an intercessor (18:20, "I stood before you to speak good for them"). The same phrase returns in verse 19, where the LORD promises that Jeremiah himself will stand before him.

decisions.choice: my soul would not be toward this people: I would have no favor or goodwill for them
decisions.reason: The soul here is the seat of desire and goodwill. To say that one's soul is not "toward" someone is to say that one's heart does not go out to them.

decisions.choice: the LORD's answer to the prayer of 14:19-22
decisions.reason: Chapter 14 ends with a plea on the people's behalf (14:19-22), after the LORD had already told Jeremiah not to pray for them (14:11; also 7:16; 11:14). Verses 1-4 are the LORD's reply: the judgment will not be turned back. The command "send them away ... let them go out" leads into the question of verse 2, "Where shall we go out?"

decisions.choice: to plead for them / and prayed for these people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say why Moses and Samuel would stand before the LORD (meaning decision m2).

source.text: וְהָיָ֛ה כִּֽי־יֹאמְר֥וּ אֵלֶ֖יךָ אָ֣נָה נֵצֵ֑א וְאָמַרְתָּ֨ אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר לַמָּ֤וֶת לַמָּ֨וֶת֙ וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר לַחֶ֨רֶב֙ לַחֶ֔רֶב וַאֲשֶׁ֤ר לָֽרָעָב֙ לָֽרָעָ֔ב וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר לַשְּׁבִ֖י לַשֶּֽׁבִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be that they say to you, Where shall we go out? and you will say to them, Thus says Yahweh: Who [are] for the death, to the death; and who [are] for the sword, to the sword; and who [are] for the famine, to the famine; and who [are] for the captivity, to the captivity.

en.L: And it will be, when they say to you, 'Where shall we go out [to]?' then you shall say to them, 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Those [who are] for death, to death; and those [who are] for the sword, to the sword; and those [who are] for famine, to famine; and those [who are] for captivity, to captivity.'
en.B: And when they ask you, 'Where are we to go?' tell them, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: Whoever is marked out for death, to death; whoever is marked out for the sword, to the sword; whoever is marked out for famine, to famine; and whoever is marked out for captivity, to captivity.'
en.R: When they ask you, 'Where can we go?' tell them, 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: Those who are meant to die will die. Those who are meant to be killed in war will be killed in war. Those who are meant to starve will starve. And those who are meant to be taken away as prisoners will be taken away.'

es.L: Y sucederá que, cuando te digan: “¿Adónde saldremos?”, les dirás: “Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Los [destinados] a la muerte, a la muerte; y los [destinados] a la espada, a la espada; y los [destinados] al hambre, al hambre; y los [destinados] al cautiverio, al cautiverio”.
es.B: Y cuando te pregunten: “¿Adónde vamos a ir?”, diles: “{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: El que está destinado a la muerte, a la muerte; el que está destinado a la espada, a la espada; el que está destinado al hambre, al hambre; y el que está destinado al cautiverio, al cautiverio”.
es.R: Cuando te pregunten: “¿Adónde podemos ir?”, diles: “Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Los que deben morir, morirán. Los que deben morir en la guerra, morirán en la guerra. Los que deben morir de hambre, morirán de hambre. Y los que deben ser llevados prisioneros, serán llevados”.

fr.L: Et s’ils te disent : “Où irons-nous ?”, tu leur diras : “Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Ceux qui [sont] pour la mort, à la mort ; et ceux qui [sont] pour l’épée, à l’épée ; et ceux qui [sont] pour la famine, à la famine ; et ceux qui [sont] pour la captivité, à la captivité.”
fr.B: Et s’ils te demandent : “Où devons-nous aller ?”, réponds-leur : “{{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Qui est destiné à la mort, à la mort ; qui est destiné à l’épée, à l’épée ; qui est destiné à la famine, à la famine ; et qui est destiné à la captivité, à la captivité.”
fr.R: S’ils te demandent : “Où pouvons-nous aller ?”, dis-leur : “Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Ceux qui doivent mourir mourront. Ceux qui doivent être tués à la guerre seront tués à la guerre. Ceux qui doivent mourir de faim mourront de faim. Et ceux qui doivent être emmenés comme prisonniers seront emmenés.”

sw.L: Na itakuwa, watakapokuambia, 'Tutatoka kwenda wapi?' ndipo utawaambia, '{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: Walio wa mauti, kwa mauti; na walio wa upanga, kwa upanga; na walio wa njaa, kwa njaa; na walio wa kutekwa, kwa kutekwa.'
sw.B: Na watakapokuuliza, 'Twende wapi?' waambie, 'Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: Aliyewekwa kwa mauti, kwa mauti; aliyewekwa kwa upanga, kwa upanga; aliyewekwa kwa njaa, kwa njaa; na aliyewekwa kwa kutekwa, kwa kutekwa.'
sw.R: Watakapokuuliza, 'Tunaweza kwenda wapi?' waambie, 'Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: Wale waliopangiwa kufa watakufa. Wale waliopangiwa kuuawa vitani watauawa vitani. Wale waliopangiwa kufa kwa njaa watakufa kwa njaa. Na wale waliopangiwa kuchukuliwa mateka watachukuliwa.'

decisions.choice: those for death, to death: each group goes to the fate set for it
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is short and without verbs: "who for death, to death". Each kind of person meets his appointed end, and no one escapes. The four fates come in a list of matching pairs, which makes the saying hard and memorable. A similar saying is spoken against Egypt in 43:11.

decisions.choice: death: probably death by disease, set beside the sword and famine
decisions.reason: Next to the sword and famine, "death" most likely means death by plague, the usual third member of the list (14:12, "sword, famine and pestilence"; compare 18:21).

decisions.choice: captivity: being taken away as prisoners into exile
decisions.reason: The last fate is to be carried off by the enemy, as Judah was taken to Babylon (13:17-19; 2 Kings 24:14-16).

decisions.choice: Where shall we go out?: the people's question, answering the command "let them go out" in verse 1
decisions.reason: The LORD has said "let them go out" (verse 1), and the people ask where they are to go. The answer is that every road leads to one of the four fates.

decisions.choice: sword: "the sword" (Literal, Balanced), "killed in war" (Readable)
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in the book, Readable says "war" for the sword and "starve" for famine, and turns the verbless phrases into short sentences.

decisions.choice: the people's question and the prophet's answer in single quotation marks
decisions.reason: They are speech inside the LORD's speech, which opened with double quotation marks in verse 1.

decisions.choice: “ ” for the people's question and the prophet's answer inside God's words
decisions.reason: The quotations inside God's speech take “ ”, where the English uses single quotes.

source.text: וּפָקַדְתִּ֨י עֲלֵיהֶ֜ם אַרְבַּ֤ע מִשְׁפָּחוֹת֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה אֶת־הַחֶ֣רֶב לַֽהֲרֹ֔ג וְאֶת־הַכְּלָבִ֖ים לִסְחֹ֑ב וְאֶת־ע֧וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֛יִם וְאֶת־בֶּהֱמַ֥ת הָאָ֖רֶץ לֶאֱכֹ֥ל וּלְהַשְׁחִֽית׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will appoint over them four kinds, declares Yahweh: the sword to kill, and the dogs to drag, and [the] birds of the heavens and [the] beasts of the earth to devour and to destroy.

en.L: And I will appoint over them four kinds, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: the sword to kill, and the dogs to drag away, and the birds of the heavens and the beasts of the earth to devour and to destroy.
en.B: Over them I will set four kinds of destroyers, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: the sword to kill, dogs to drag them off, and the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth to devour and destroy.
en.R: I will send four kinds of destroyers against them, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: war to kill them, dogs to drag away their bodies, and birds and wild animals to eat what is left and finish them off.

es.L: Y pondré sobre ellos cuatro clases, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: la espada para matar, y los perros para arrastrar, y las aves del cielo y las bestias de la tierra para devorar y destruir.
es.B: Pondré sobre ellos cuatro clases de destructores, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: la espada para matar, los perros para arrastrarlos, y las aves del cielo y las bestias de la tierra para devorar y destruir.
es.R: Enviaré contra ellos cuatro clases de destructores, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: la guerra para matarlos, los perros para arrastrar sus cuerpos, y las aves y los animales salvajes para comerse lo que quede y acabar con ellos.

fr.L: Et j’établirai sur eux quatre espèces, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : l’épée pour tuer, et les chiens pour traîner, et les oiseaux du ciel et les bêtes de la terre pour dévorer et pour détruire.
fr.B: Je lâcherai contre eux quatre sortes de fléaux, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : l’épée pour tuer, les chiens pour les traîner, les oiseaux du ciel et les bêtes de la terre pour dévorer et détruire.
fr.R: J’enverrai contre eux quatre sortes de destructeurs, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : la guerre pour les tuer, les chiens pour traîner leurs corps, et les oiseaux et les bêtes sauvages pour manger ce qui reste et les faire disparaître.

sw.L: Nami nitaweka juu yao aina nne, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}: upanga kuua, na mbwa kukokota, na ndege wa angani na wanyama wa nchi kula na kuharibu.
sw.B: Juu yao nitaweka aina nne za waangamizaji, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}: upanga kuua, mbwa kuwakokota, na ndege wa angani na wanyama wa nchi kula na kuangamiza.
sw.R: Nitatuma aina nne za waangamizaji dhidi yao, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}: vita kuwaua, mbwa kukokota maiti zao, na ndege na wanyama wa porini kula kilichobaki na kuwamaliza.

decisions.choice: kinds: classes or sorts of destroyers
decisions.reason: The word usually means clans or families. Here it groups the four things that will destroy the people: one that kills and three that devour the dead.

decisions.choice: appoint over them: assign to them as a punishment
decisions.reason: The verb, which often means "visit" or "punish", here means to put someone in charge over another, as officers are appointed. The LORD sets these four over the people as their masters.

decisions.choice: dogs, birds and wild animals: the dead are left unburied
decisions.reason: To lie unburied, food for dogs, birds and beasts, was the worst disgrace in Israel and a curse of the covenant (Deuteronomy 28:26; 1 Kings 14:11; Jeremiah 7:33; 16:4). Dogs in the towns were scavengers, not pets.

decisions.choice: four kinds of destroyers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the four kinds are, as the list that follows shows.

decisions.choice: war to kill them ... drag away their bodies ... eat what is left
decisions.reason: Readable says "war" for the sword, as the book does in lists like this, and says plainly that the animals take the bodies of the dead.

source.text: וּנְתַתִּ֣ים לְזַֽעֲוָ֔ה לְכֹ֖ל מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הָאָ֑רֶץ בִּ֠גְלַל מְנַשֶּׁ֤ה בֶן־יְחִזְקִיָּ֨הוּ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה עַ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֖ה בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will make them into a horror to all [the] kingdoms of the earth because of Manasseh son of Hezekiah king of Judah, for what he did in Jerusalem.

en.L: And I will make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth, because of Manasseh son of Hezekiah king of Judah, for what he did in Jerusalem."
en.B: Because of Manasseh son of Hezekiah, king of Judah, and what he did in Jerusalem, I will make them a horror to every kingdom on earth."
en.R: I will make them something that horrifies every kingdom on earth. This will happen because of the things that Manasseh son of Hezekiah, king of Judah, did in Jerusalem."

es.L: Y los convertiré en espanto para todos los reinos de la tierra, a causa de Manasés hijo de Ezequías, rey de Judá, por lo que hizo en Jerusalén».
es.B: A causa de Manasés hijo de Ezequías, rey de Judá, y de lo que hizo en Jerusalén, los convertiré en un espanto para todos los reinos de la tierra».
es.R: Haré que todos los reinos de la tierra se horroricen al verlos. Esto sucederá por las cosas que hizo en Jerusalén Manasés hijo de Ezequías, rey de Judá».

fr.L: Et je ferai d’eux un objet d’horreur pour tous les royaumes de la terre, à cause de Manassé fils d’Ézéchias, roi de Juda, pour ce qu’il a fait à Jérusalem. »
fr.B: À cause de Manassé, fils d’Ézéchias, roi de Juda, et de ce qu’il a fait à Jérusalem, je ferai d’eux un objet d’horreur pour tous les royaumes de la terre. »
fr.R: Je ferai d’eux un peuple qui horrifie tous les royaumes de la terre. Cela arrivera à cause de ce que Manassé fils d’Ézéchias, roi de Juda, a fait à Jérusalem. »

sw.L: Nami nitawafanya kuwa kitisho kwa falme zote za dunia, kwa sababu ya Manase mwana wa Hezekia mfalme wa Yuda, kwa ajili ya aliyoyatenda katika Yerusalemu."
sw.B: Kwa sababu ya Manase mwana wa Hezekia, mfalme wa Yuda, na yale aliyoyatenda katika Yerusalemu, nitawafanya kuwa kitisho kwa kila ufalme duniani."
sw.R: Nitawafanya kuwa kitu kinachotisha kila ufalme duniani. Hili litatokea kwa sababu ya mambo ambayo Manase mwana wa Hezekia, mfalme wa Yuda, aliyatenda katika Yerusalemu."

decisions.choice: horror: the form the scribes noted in the margin to be read
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text spells this word slightly differently from the form the scribes noted in the margin to be read aloud. The meaning is the same either way: something that makes people tremble.

decisions.choice: a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth: the curse of Deuteronomy 28:25
decisions.reason: The same words appear among the curses of the covenant: "you will be a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth" (Deuteronomy 28:25). What happens to Judah will make other nations shudder. The phrase returns in 24:9; 29:18; 34:17.

decisions.choice: because of Manasseh: the sins of King Manasseh in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Manasseh, Hezekiah's son, reigned fifty-five years and filled Jerusalem with idols, altars to other gods and innocent blood (2 Kings 21:1-16). 2 Kings 23:26-27 and 24:3-4 say that the LORD's anger against Judah did not turn away because of what Manasseh had done, even after Josiah's reforms.

decisions.choice: Manasseh's sin and the people's own guilt
decisions.reason: The judgment is not on the king's sin alone. The people followed him (2 Kings 21:9) and went on in the same ways, as verse 6 says: "You have rejected me." Manasseh's reign marks how deep the nation's sin had gone.

decisions.choice: Because of Manasseh ... first
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the cause first, so that the sentence ends on the judgment.

decisions.choice: something that horrifies every kingdom on earth. This will happen because of ...
decisions.reason: Readable splits the sentence in two and says plainly that the other nations will be horrified at what happens to the people.

decisions.choice: "Manasés hijo de Ezequías"
decisions.reason: The king's names as published in 2 Kings 20-21.

decisions.choice: "Manassé fils d’Ézéchias"
decisions.reason: The forms of the French Kings.

source.text: כִּ֠י מִֽי־יַחְמֹ֤ל עָלַ֨יִךְ֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וּמִ֖י יָנ֣וּד לָ֑ךְ וּמִ֣י יָס֔וּר לִשְׁאֹ֥ל לְשָׁלֹ֖ם לָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: For who will have pity on you, Jerusalem, and who will show sympathy to you, and who will turn aside to ask about your welfare?

en.L: For who will have pity on you, Jerusalem, \q and who will show you sympathy? \q And who will turn aside to ask after your welfare?
en.B: Who will take pity on you, Jerusalem? \q Who will grieve over you? \q Who will turn aside to ask how you are?
en.R: Jerusalem, who will feel sorry for you? \q Who will cry for you? \q Who will even stop to ask how you are doing?

es.L: Porque ¿quién tendrá compasión de ti, Jerusalén, \q y quién se dolerá de ti? \q ¿Y quién se desviará para preguntar por tu bienestar?
es.B: ¿Quién tendrá piedad de ti, Jerusalén? \q ¿Quién llorará por ti? \q ¿Quién se apartará del camino para preguntarte cómo estás?
es.R: Jerusalén, ¿quién sentirá lástima por ti? \q ¿Quién llorará por ti? \q ¿Quién se detendrá siquiera a preguntarte cómo estás?

fr.L: Car qui aura pitié de toi, Jérusalem, \q et qui te plaindra ? \q Et qui se détournera pour s’informer de ta paix ?
fr.B: Qui aura pitié de toi, Jérusalem ? \q Qui pleurera sur toi ? \q Qui fera un détour pour demander comment tu vas ?
fr.R: Jérusalem, qui aura pitié de toi ? \q Qui pleurera pour toi ? \q Qui s’arrêtera même pour te demander comment tu vas ?

sw.L: Kwa maana ni nani atakayekuhurumia, Yerusalemu, \q na ni nani atakayekuombolezea? \q Na ni nani atakayegeuka kando kuuliza habari za hali yako?
sw.B: Ni nani atakayekuonea huruma, Yerusalemu? \q Ni nani atakayekuombolezea? \q Ni nani atakayegeuka kando kukuuliza hali yako?
sw.R: Yerusalemu, ni nani atakayekuonea huruma? \q Ni nani atakayekulilia? \q Ni nani atakayesimama hata kukusalimu?

decisions.choice: the LORD speaks to Jerusalem: his speech continues in poetry
decisions.reason: The LORD, who has been speaking since verse 1, now turns to Jerusalem itself, addressed as a woman (the words for "you" are feminine). Verses 5-9 are a poem of judgment in the LORD's own voice. The word "for" links it to what goes before: no one will pity the city, because its fate is sealed.

decisions.choice: grieve for you: show sympathy by mourning
alternatives: shake the head at you (in scorn)
decisions.reason: The verb means to sway or shake the head, the gestures of mourning and comfort (Job 2:11; 42:11). Jeremiah is later told not to go and mourn for the people (16:5).

decisions.choice: ask about your welfare: ask how you are, greet you
decisions.reason: To ask about someone's peace (shalom) is to greet them and ask after their well-being (Exodus 18:7; Judges 18:15). No one will even stop to greet the city.

decisions.choice: no quotation marks from verse 5 on
decisions.reason: Verses 1-4 are prose, and the LORD's words there are quoted as prose quotes speech. From verse 5 the LORD speaks in poetry, and, as in the poetry of the prophets elsewhere, his first-person speech takes no quotation marks; nor do Jeremiah's prayer and the LORD's answers in verses 10-21.

decisions.choice: "For" kept at Literal, left out at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: The link to verses 1-4 is clear from the context, and three questions in a row read more naturally without it.

source.text: אַ֣תְּ נָטַ֥שְׁתְּ אֹתִ֛י נְאֻם־יְהוָ֖ה אָח֣וֹר תֵּלֵ֑כִי וָאַ֨ט אֶת־יָדִ֤י עָלַ֨יִךְ֙ וָֽאַשְׁחִיתֵ֔ךְ נִלְאֵ֖יתִי הִנָּחֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: You, you have abandoned me, declares Yahweh, backward you go; and I stretched out my hand against you and destroyed you; I am weary of relenting.

en.L: You, you have forsaken {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; backward you keep going. \q So I stretched out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand against you and destroyed you; \q I have grown weary of relenting.
en.B: You have rejected {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; you keep turning your back. \q So I have reached out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand against you and destroyed you; \q I am tired of relenting.
en.R: You have turned away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. You keep going the wrong way. \q So I have raised {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand against you and destroyed you. \q I am tired of holding back {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} punishment.

es.L: Tú {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} has abandonado, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}; hacia atrás sigues andando. \q Por eso extendí {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano contra ti y te destruí; \q estoy cansado de retractarme.
es.B: Tú {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} has rechazado, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}; sigues dándome la espalda. \q Por eso he extendido {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano contra ti y te he destruido; \q estoy cansado de contenerme.
es.R: Tú te has apartado de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Sigues yendo por mal camino. \q Por eso he levantado {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano contra ti y te he destruido. \q Estoy cansado de retener {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} castigo.

fr.L: Toi, tu {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as délaissé, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ; tu vas en arrière. \q Alors j’ai étendu {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} main contre toi et je t’ai détruite ; \q je suis las de revenir sur {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} décision.
fr.B: Tu {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as rejeté, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ; tu ne cesses de tourner le dos. \q Alors j’ai étendu {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} main contre toi et je t’ai détruite ; \q je suis fatigué de revenir sur {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} décision.
fr.R: Tu t’es détournée de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Tu continues à aller dans la mauvaise direction. \q Alors j’ai levé {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} main contre toi et je t’ai détruite. \q Je suis fatigué de retenir {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} punition.

sw.L: Wewe, umeniacha, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; unaendelea kurudi nyuma. \q Kwa hiyo nimeunyosha mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} juu yako na kukuangamiza; \q nimechoka kughairi.
sw.B: Umenikataa, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; unaendelea kunipa kisogo. \q Kwa hiyo nimeunyosha mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} dhidi yako na kukuangamiza; \q nimechoka kughairi.
sw.R: Umeniacha, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Unaendelea kwenda njia mbaya. \q Kwa hiyo nimeinua mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} dhidi yako na kukuangamiza. \q Nimechoka kuizuia adhabu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.

decisions.choice: you have forsaken me: you have abandoned and rejected me
decisions.reason: The verb means to leave or cast off. The pronoun "you" is written out for emphasis: the fault is Jerusalem's own.

decisions.choice: you keep going backward: turning away from God instead of toward him
decisions.reason: Going backward is the opposite of following the LORD (7:24, "they went backward and not forward"). The verb form describes something the city keeps doing.

decisions.choice: I have stretched out my hand ... and destroyed you: the judgment is spoken of as done
decisions.reason: The verbs are past in form. They may look back on disasters that have already struck, or speak of the coming destruction as so certain that it is already done, as the prophets often do. The same is true of verses 7-9.

decisions.choice: I am weary of relenting: tired of turning back from punishment
alternatives: I am weary of showing pity
decisions.reason: To relent is to change one's mind about a punishment one has announced (18:8; 26:3; Amos 7:3, 6). The LORD has held back again and again; now he will not.

decisions.choice: holding back my punishment
decisions.reason: Readable says what the LORD has been relenting from (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: "retractarme" (L); "contenerme" (B); "retener mi castigo" (R)
decisions.reason: God's relenting is never "arrepentirse", as in 4:28.

source.text: וָאֶזְרֵ֥ם בְּמִזְרֶ֖ה בְּשַׁעֲרֵ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ שִׁכַּ֤לְתִּי אִבַּ֨דְתִּי֙ אֶת־עַמִּ֔י מִדַּרְכֵיהֶ֖ם לוֹא־שָֽׁבוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I have winnowed them with a winnowing fork in [the] gates of the land; I have bereaved, I have destroyed my people; from their ways they did not turn.

en.L: And I have winnowed them with a winnowing fork in the gates of the land; \q I have bereaved [them], I have destroyed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people; \q from their ways they did not turn.
en.B: With a winnowing fork I have scattered them at the gates of the land. \q I have taken their children and destroyed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, \q because they did not turn from their ways.
en.R: I have scattered them like chaff blown away from the grain, in the towns of the land. \q I have taken away their children and destroyed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, \q because they would not stop living the way they did.

es.L: Y los he aventado con el bieldo en las puertas de la tierra; \q he dejado sin hijos, he destruido a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo; \q de sus caminos no se volvieron.
es.B: Con el bieldo los he dispersado en las puertas del país. \q Les he quitado los hijos y he destruido a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo, \q porque no se volvieron de sus caminos.
es.R: Los he dispersado como la paja que se separa del grano, en las ciudades del país. \q Les he quitado sus hijos y he destruido a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo, \q porque no quisieron dejar su manera de vivir.

fr.L: Et je les ai vannés avec la fourche aux portes du pays ; \q j’ai privé d’enfants, j’ai détruit {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple ; \q ils ne sont pas revenus de leurs voies.
fr.B: Avec la fourche à vanner, je les ai dispersés aux portes du pays. \q J’ai pris leurs enfants et détruit {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple, \q parce qu’ils ne sont pas revenus de leurs voies.
fr.R: Je les ai dispersés comme la paille qu’on sépare du grain, dans les villes du pays. \q J’ai pris leurs enfants et détruit {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple, \q parce qu’ils n’ont pas voulu changer de conduite.

sw.L: Nami nimewapepeta kwa uma wa kupepetea katika malango ya nchi; \q nimewafiwisha [watoto], nimewaangamiza watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}; \q hawakurudi kutoka njia zao.
sw.B: Kwa uma wa kupepetea nimewatawanya katika malango ya nchi. \q Nimewaondolea watoto wao na kuwaangamiza watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, \q kwa sababu hawakugeuka kuacha njia zao.
sw.R: Nimewatawanya kama makapi yanavyopeperushwa mbali na nafaka, katika miji ya nchi. \q Nimewaondolea watoto wao na kuwaangamiza watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, \q kwa sababu hawakutaka kuacha njia zao.

decisions.choice: winnowed them with a winnowing fork: scattered them as chaff is scattered
decisions.reason: At harvest, threshed grain was tossed into the air with a wooden fork so that the wind blew the chaff away. The picture is of the people being scattered and blown away (4:11; 13:24; 51:2; Isaiah 41:16).

decisions.choice: the gates of the land: probably the towns of the land
alternatives: the entrances or borders of the land
decisions.reason: A town was often named by its gates, where its business was done (Deuteronomy 12:12, "within your gates"). The phrase may instead mean the entrances or borders of the country, as in Nahum 3:13.

decisions.choice: bereaved: made childless
decisions.reason: The verb means to take away someone's children by death. Families lose their sons, as verses 8-9 go on to say.

decisions.choice: from their ways they did not turn: the reason for the judgment
alternatives: yet even so they did not turn from their ways
decisions.reason: The last clause has no linking word. It most naturally gives the cause: the people were struck because they would not turn back. It may also mean that even after these blows they did not turn.

decisions.choice: because they did not turn
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply "because" to show the link the Hebrew leaves unstated (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: scattered them like chaff ... in the towns of the land
decisions.reason: Readable explains the farming picture and gives the sense of "gates" (meaning decisions m1 and m2).

source.text: עָֽצְמוּ־לִ֤י אַלְמְנֹתָו֙מֵח֣וֹל יַמִּ֔ים הֵבֵ֨אתִי לָהֶ֥ם עַל־אֵ֛ם בָּח֖וּר שֹׁדֵ֣ד בַּֽצָּהֳרָ֑יִם הִפַּ֤לְתִּי עָלֶ֨יהָ֙ פִּתְאֹ֔ם עִ֖יר וּבֶהָלֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: Numerous to me [were] its widows more than [the] sand of [the] seas; I have brought to them, against [the] mother of [the] young man, a destroyer at noon; I have made fall on her suddenly anguish and terrors.

en.L: Its widows have become more numerous before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} than the sand of the seas; \q I have brought against them, against the mother of young men, a destroyer at noon. \q I have made anguish and terrors fall on her suddenly.
en.B: Before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} their widows have become more than the sand of the seas. \q At noon I have brought a destroyer against them, against the mothers of young men; \q I have made anguish and terror fall on them suddenly.
en.R: I have seen their widows become more than the grains of sand by the sea. \q In the middle of the day I brought a destroyer against the mothers of young men. \q Suddenly I made pain and terror fall on them.

es.L: Sus viudas se han multiplicado delante de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} más que la arena de los mares; \q he traído contra ellos, contra la madre del joven, un destructor al mediodía. \q He hecho caer sobre ella de repente angustia y terrores.
es.B: Delante de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} sus viudas son más que la arena de los mares. \q Al mediodía he traído un destructor contra ellos, contra las madres de los jóvenes; \q he hecho caer sobre ellas de repente angustia y terror.
es.R: He visto que sus viudas son más que los granos de arena junto al mar. \q En pleno día traje un destructor contra las madres de los jóvenes. \q De repente hice caer sobre ellas dolor y terror.

fr.L: Ses veuves sont devenues pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} plus nombreuses que le sable des mers ; \q j’ai fait venir sur eux, sur la mère du jeune homme, le dévastateur en plein midi. \q J’ai fait tomber sur elle soudain l’angoisse et les terreurs.
fr.B: Devant {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, leurs veuves sont devenues plus nombreuses que le sable des mers. \q En plein midi, j’ai fait venir un dévastateur contre eux, contre les mères des jeunes gens ; \q j’ai fait tomber sur elles, tout à coup, l’angoisse et la terreur.
fr.R: J’ai vu leurs veuves devenir plus nombreuses que les grains de sable au bord de la mer. \q En plein jour, j’ai fait venir un destructeur contre les mères des jeunes gens. \q Tout à coup, j’ai fait tomber sur elles la douleur et la terreur.

sw.L: Wajane wake wamekuwa wengi mbele {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kuliko mchanga wa bahari; \q nimeleta juu yao, juu ya mama wa vijana, mwangamizaji adhuhuri. \q Nimemwangushia ghafla fadhaa na vitisho.
sw.B: Mbele {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} wajane wao wamekuwa wengi kuliko mchanga wa bahari. \q Adhuhuri nimeleta mwangamizaji juu yao, juu ya mama wa vijana; \q nimewaangushia ghafla fadhaa na vitisho.
sw.R: Nimeona wajane wao wakiwa wengi kuliko chembe za mchanga ufuoni mwa bahari. \q Katikati ya mchana nilileta mwangamizaji dhidi ya mama wa vijana. \q Ghafla niliwaangushia maumivu na hofu kuu.

decisions.choice: more than the sand of the seas: the promise of countless descendants turned around
decisions.reason: God promised Abraham descendants as many as the sand on the seashore (Genesis 22:17; 32:13). Now it is the widows who cannot be counted.

decisions.choice: before me: in my sight, as I count them
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "to me". The LORD sees the widows multiply; since he is the one bringing the destroyer, it may also mean "because of me".

decisions.choice: against the mother of young men: the mothers of the young men who fall in battle
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is very short: "against mother, young man". It most likely means the mothers who lose their grown sons, which leads into the mother of seven in verse 9. It could also mean "against mother and young man", both alike.

decisions.choice: a destroyer at noon: an attack when no one expects it
decisions.reason: In the heat of midday people rested, and an attack then came as a shock (6:4; 2 Samuel 4:5).

decisions.choice: anguish: agitation, alarm
alternatives: a city (an enemy city) and terrors
decisions.reason: The word is rare in this sense; it is spelled like the common word for "city". Most take it as a word for alarm or agitation, paired with "terrors".

decisions.choice: At noon I have brought a destroyer
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the time first and uses "them" for the collective "her", the mothers.

source.text: אֻמְלְלָ֞ה יֹלֶ֣דֶת הַשִּׁבְעָ֗ה נָפְחָ֥ה נַפְשָׁ֛הּ בָּ֥א שִׁמְשָׁ֛הּ בְּעֹ֥ד יוֹמָ֖ם בּ֣וֹשָׁה וְחָפֵ֑רָה וּשְׁאֵֽרִיתָ֗ם לַחֶ֧רֶב אֶתֵּ֛ן לִפְנֵ֥י אֹיְבֵיהֶ֖ם נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: She has languished, she who bore the seven; she has breathed out her soul; her sun has gone down while yet [it is] day; she is ashamed and disgraced; and [the] rest of them to the sword I will give before their enemies, declares Yahweh.

en.L: Languishing is she who bore seven; she has breathed out her life; her sun has gone down while [it was] still day; she is put to shame and abashed. \q And their remnant I will give to the sword before their enemies, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: The mother of seven grows faint and gasps out her life; her sun has set while it is still day; she is shamed and humiliated. \q And those of them who remain I will give to the sword before their enemies, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: A mother who had seven children grows weak and can hardly breathe. Her sun has gone down in the middle of the day, and she is full of shame and disgrace. \q Those who are still alive I will let their enemies kill in war, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Desfallece la que dio a luz siete; ha exhalado su vida; su sol se puso siendo aún de día; está avergonzada y confundida. \q Y a su remanente lo entregaré a la espada delante de sus enemigos, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: La madre de siete hijos desfallece y exhala su vida; su sol se ha puesto cuando aún era de día; está avergonzada y humillada. \q Y a los que queden de ellos los entregaré a la espada delante de sus enemigos, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Una madre que tuvo siete hijos se debilita y casi no puede respirar. Su sol se ha puesto en pleno día, y está llena de vergüenza y deshonra. \q A los que todavía quedan con vida dejaré que sus enemigos los maten en la guerra, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Elle languit, celle qui avait enfanté sept [fils] ; elle a rendu l’âme ; son soleil s’est couché pendant qu’il [faisait] encore jour ; elle est honteuse et confuse. \q Et ce qui reste d’eux, je le livrerai à l’épée devant leurs ennemis, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: La mère de sept enfants dépérit et rend son dernier souffle ; son soleil s’est couché en plein jour ; elle est couverte de honte et d’humiliation. \q Et ceux d’entre eux qui restent, je les livrerai à l’épée devant leurs ennemis, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Une mère qui avait sept enfants devient faible et ne peut presque plus respirer. Son soleil s’est couché au milieu de la journée, et elle est pleine de honte et d’humiliation. \q Ceux qui sont encore en vie, je laisserai leurs ennemis les tuer à la guerre, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Amedhoofika yule aliyezaa saba; ameitoa roho yake; jua lake limekuchwa kungali [ni] mchana; ameaibishwa na kufedheheka. \q Na mabaki yao nitawatoa kwa upanga mbele ya adui zao, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Mama wa watoto saba anazimia na kukata roho; jua lake limetua kungali mchana; ameaibishwa na kudhalilishwa. \q Na wale waliobaki kati yao nitawatoa kwa upanga mbele ya adui zao, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Mama aliyekuwa na watoto saba anadhoofika na hawezi kupumua. Jua lake limetua katikati ya mchana, naye amejaa aibu na fedheha. \q Wale ambao bado wako hai nitawaacha adui zao wawaue vitani, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

decisions.choice: she who bore seven: a mother blessed with a full family
decisions.reason: Seven children stood for a complete and blessed family (Ruth 4:15; 1 Samuel 2:5, where "the barren has borne seven"). Here the blessing is reversed: the mother loses all her sons.

decisions.choice: breathed out her life: gasps for breath, faints away
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean that she dies, or that she gasps for breath in grief and despair (Job 31:39). Either way her life is drained out of her.

decisions.choice: her sun has gone down while it is still day: her joy and hope end long before their time
decisions.reason: Her sons were the light of her life. They have died young, so it is dark for her at midday (compare Amos 8:9).

decisions.choice: has gone down: the form the scribes noted in the margin to be read
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text and the form noted in the margin differ only in a letter that marks the verb as masculine or feminine (the word for "sun" can be either). The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: the rest of them: those who survive the first disasters
decisions.reason: Even the survivors will not escape: they too will fall by the sword.

decisions.choice: kill in war
decisions.reason: Readable says "war" for the sword, as the book does elsewhere.

source.text: אֽוֹי־לִ֣י אִמִּ֔י כִּ֣י יְלִדְתִּ֗נִי אִ֥ישׁ רִ֛יב וְאִ֥ישׁ מָד֖וֹן לְכָל־הָאָ֑רֶץ לֹֽא־נָשִׁ֥יתִי וְלֹא־נָֽשׁוּ־בִ֖י כֻּלֹּ֥ה מְקַלְלַֽונִי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Woe to me, my mother, that you bore me, a man of strife and a man of contention to all the land; not I have lent and not they have lent to me, all of him cursing me.

en.L: Woe [is] me, my mother, \q that you bore me, a man of strife and a man of contention to all the land! \q I have not lent, and they have not lent to me, [yet] all of them curse me.
en.B: Woe is me, my mother, \q that you gave birth to me, a man the whole land strives and quarrels with! \q I have not lent money, and no one has lent money to me, yet every one of them curses me.
en.R: How terrible this is for me, my mother! \q You gave birth to me, and now everyone in the land argues and fights with me. \q I have not lent anyone money, and I have not borrowed from anyone, but all of them curse me.

es.L: ¡Ay de mí, madre mía, \q que me diste a luz, hombre de contienda y hombre de discordia para toda la tierra! \q No he prestado, ni me han prestado, [y] todos me maldicen.
es.B: ¡Ay de mí, madre mía, \q que me diste a luz, un hombre con quien toda la tierra pelea y discute! \q No he prestado dinero, ni nadie me ha prestado a mí, y sin embargo todos me maldicen.
es.R: ¡Qué terrible es esto para mí, madre mía! \q Me diste a luz, y ahora todos en el país discuten y pelean conmigo. \q No le he prestado dinero a nadie, ni le he pedido prestado a nadie, pero todos me maldicen.

fr.L: Malheur à moi, ma mère, \q de ce que tu m’as enfanté, homme de querelle et homme de dispute pour tout le pays ! \q Je n’ai pas prêté, et on ne m’a pas prêté, [et pourtant] tous me maudissent.
fr.B: Malheur à moi, ma mère, \q de ce que tu m’as mis au monde, un homme avec qui tout le pays se querelle et se dispute ! \q Je n’ai pas prêté d’argent, et personne ne m’en a prêté, et pourtant tous me maudissent.
fr.R: Quel malheur pour moi, ma mère ! \q Tu m’as mis au monde, et maintenant tout le monde dans le pays se dispute et se bat avec moi. \q Je n’ai prêté d’argent à personne et je n’ai rien emprunté à personne, mais tous me maudissent.

sw.L: Ole wangu, mama yangu, \q kwamba ulinizaa, mtu wa ugomvi na mtu wa mashindano kwa nchi yote! \q Sijakopesha, wala hawajanikopesha, [lakini] wote wananilaani.
sw.B: Ole wangu, mama yangu, \q kwamba ulinizaa, mtu ambaye nchi yote inashindana na kugombana naye! \q Sijamkopesha mtu fedha, wala hakuna aliyenikopesha, lakini kila mmoja wao ananilaani.
sw.R: Mambo ni mabaya sana kwangu, mama yangu! \q Ulinizaa, na sasa kila mtu katika nchi anabishana na kupigana nami. \q Sijamkopesha mtu yeyote fedha, wala sijakopa kwa mtu yeyote, lakini wote wananilaani.

decisions.choice: the start of Jeremiah's second lament: his prayer to God about his suffering as a prophet
decisions.reason: Verses 10-21 are the second of Jeremiah's prayers of complaint (the others are 11:18-12:6; 17:14-18; 18:18-23; 20:7-18). The prophet pours out his pain, and the LORD answers him (verses 11-14 and 19-21). Here he begins by crying out to his mother, but from verse 15 he speaks directly to God.

decisions.choice: my mother, that you bore me: a cry of grief that he was ever born
decisions.reason: Jeremiah does not blame his mother. Addressing her is a way of mourning his own birth, as he does more fiercely in 20:14-18 (compare Job 3:1-3). He had been set apart for this work before he was born (1:5).

decisions.choice: a man of strife and contention to all the land: a man the whole land quarrels with
decisions.reason: The phrase does not mean that Jeremiah loves to quarrel. It means that his message has made him the one everyone in the land argues with, as the LORD warned in 1:18-19.

decisions.choice: I have not lent and no one has lent to me: I have given no cause for anyone to hate me
decisions.reason: Lending and borrowing were common causes of bitter quarrels between neighbors (Deuteronomy 24:10-13; Nehemiah 5:1-7). Jeremiah has had no such dealings, yet he is cursed as if he had cheated everyone.

decisions.choice: all of them curse me: the usual reading of an unusual form
decisions.reason: The Hebrew letters here form an unusual combination, literally "all of him cursing me". Divided differently, the same letters read "all of them curse me", which fits the sense. The meaning is clear either way.

decisions.choice: lent money ... borrowed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say that the lending is of money, and Readable turns "they have not lent to me" into "I have not borrowed".

decisions.choice: Woe is me / How terrible this is for me
decisions.reason: The cry of grief spoken of oneself is rendered as in Isaiah 6:5.

decisions.choice: "¡Ay de mí!" (L, B); "¡Qué terrible es esto para mí!" (R)
decisions.reason: Woe said of oneself, as the terms note sets it for Spanish. This opens Jeremiah's second lament (15:10-21), his own prayer about his suffering as a prophet.

decisions.choice: first person, no quotation marks
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's second lament (15:10-21) is his prayer and is set without quotation marks, as at 11:18 (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: tenses of speech in Jeremiah's lament (15:10-21)
decisions.reason: As in 11:18-12:6, Jeremiah's lament is his prayer and takes the tenses of speech at every level.

source.text: אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אִם־לֹ֥א שֵֽׁרִיתִ֖יךָלְט֑וֹב אִם־ל֣וֹא׀הִפְגַּ֣עְתִּֽי בְךָ֗ בְּעֵ֥ת־רָעָ֛ה וּבְעֵ֥ת צָרָ֖ה אֶת־הָאֹיֵֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: Said Yahweh: Surely I will set you free for good; surely I will make plead with you in [the] time of evil and in [the] time of distress the enemy.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said: \q Surely I will set you free for good; \q surely I will make the enemy plead with you in a time of disaster and in a time of distress.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said: \q I will surely set you free for your good; \q I will surely make your enemy come to you pleading in the time of disaster, in the time of distress.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered: \q I will certainly set you free and do good to you. \q When disaster and hard times come, I will make your enemies come to you and beg for your help.

es.L: Dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: \q Ciertamente te libraré para bien; \q ciertamente haré que el enemigo te suplique en el tiempo de la desgracia y en el tiempo de la angustia.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo: \q Te libraré, sin duda, para tu bien; \q sin duda haré que tu enemigo venga a suplicarte en el tiempo de la desgracia, en el tiempo de la angustia.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} respondió: \q Ciertamente te liberaré y te haré bien. \q Cuando lleguen la desgracia y los tiempos difíciles, haré que tus enemigos vengan a ti a pedirte ayuda.

fr.L: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit : \q Certainement je te délivrerai pour le bien ; \q certainement je ferai que l’ennemi vienne te supplier au temps du malheur et au temps de la détresse.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit : \q Oui, je te libérerai pour ton bien ; \q oui, je ferai venir ton ennemi te supplier au temps du malheur, au temps de la détresse.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a répondu : \q Je te libérerai, c’est sûr, et je te ferai du bien. \q Quand viendront le malheur et les temps difficiles, je ferai venir tes ennemis vers toi pour qu’ils te supplient de les aider.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akasema: \q Hakika nitakuachilia kwa ajili ya mema; \q hakika nitamfanya adui akusihi wakati wa mabaya na wakati wa dhiki.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akasema: \q Hakika nitakuweka huru kwa ajili ya mema yako; \q hakika nitamfanya adui yako aje kwako akikusihi wakati wa maafa, wakati wa dhiki.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akajibu: \q Hakika nitakuweka huru na kukutendea mema. \q Maafa na nyakati ngumu zitakapokuja, nitawafanya adui zako waje kwako wakiomba msaada wako.

decisions.choice: The LORD said: the LORD answers Jeremiah
alternatives: So be it, Lord: Jeremiah's words, protesting that he served God and prayed for his enemies
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has "The LORD said", and what follows is the LORD's answer to Jeremiah's cry. The Greek translation reads instead "So be it, Lord" and makes the verse Jeremiah's own words: "So be it, Lord, if I did not serve you for good, if I did not stand before you in the time of trouble for my enemy." Verses 11-14 are among the hardest in the book, and every reading is uncertain. These statements about the Greek are made from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: I will set you free: I will release you for good
alternatives: I will strengthen you for good
your remnant will be for good
decisions.reason: The word is unusual, and the written text and the form the scribes noted in the margin differ. It is taken from a verb meaning to loose or set free. Others link it to a word meaning "strengthen", or to the word for "remnant" ("your remnant will be for good").

decisions.choice: surely ... surely: the LORD's solemn promise
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "if not ... if not" is the form of an oath, meaning "surely". If the verse is Jeremiah's words (meaning decision m1), the same form would be his protest: "Did I not ...?"

decisions.choice: make the enemy plead with you: those who oppose Jeremiah will come to him for help
alternatives: I pleaded with you on behalf of the enemy
decisions.reason: The verb means to meet or entreat. Later the king and the people who had rejected Jeremiah came to ask him to pray for them (21:1-2; 37:3; 42:1-3). The verse could also mean "I will make the enemy deal kindly with you", or, as Jeremiah's words, "I pleaded with you for the enemy".

decisions.choice: your enemy ... for your good / your enemies ... beg for your help
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose enemy is meant and for whose good the LORD acts. Readable says "answered" to show that the LORD replies to verse 10.

source.text: הֲיָרֹ֨עַ בַּרְזֶ֧ל׀בַּרְזֶ֛ל מִצָּפ֖וֹן וּנְחֹֽשֶׁת׃

records.literal_gloss: Can it break, iron, iron from [the] north and bronze?

en.L: Can [anyone] break iron, iron from the north, and bronze?
en.B: Can anyone smash iron, iron from the north, or bronze?
en.R: Can anyone break iron, the hard iron from the north, or bronze?

es.L: ¿Puede [alguien] quebrar el hierro, el hierro del norte, y el bronce?
es.B: ¿Puede alguien quebrar el hierro, el hierro del norte, o el bronce?
es.R: ¿Puede alguien romper el hierro, el hierro duro del norte, o el bronce?

fr.L: Brise-t-on le fer, le fer du nord, et le bronze ?
fr.B: Peut-on briser le fer, le fer du nord, ou le bronze ?
fr.R: Quelqu’un peut-il briser le fer, le fer dur qui vient du nord, ou le bronze ?

sw.L: Je, [mtu] aweza kuvunja chuma, chuma kutoka kaskazini, na shaba?
sw.B: Je, kuna mtu awezaye kuvunja chuma, chuma kutoka kaskazini, au shaba?
sw.R: Je, kuna mtu anayeweza kuvunja chuma, chuma kigumu kutoka kaskazini, au shaba?

decisions.choice: iron from the north and bronze: something that cannot be broken
alternatives: Judah cannot break the northern enemy
Can iron break iron from the north?
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "No", but what the iron stands for is uncertain. It may be the enemy from the north, whom Judah cannot break (1:13-15; 6:22). Or it may be Jeremiah himself, whom the LORD made a pillar of iron and walls of bronze (1:18; 15:20), so that his enemies cannot break him. The Hebrew may also be read "Can iron break iron from the north?"

decisions.choice: iron from the north: iron of especially hard quality
decisions.reason: Iron brought from the lands north of Israel, toward the Black Sea, may have been known for its hardness. The phrase also recalls the enemy "from the north" of chapters 1-6.

decisions.choice: [anyone]
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject; Literal supplies one in brackets.

decisions.choice: the hard iron from the north
decisions.reason: Readable adds "hard" to make clear why the iron from the north is mentioned (meaning decision m2).

source.text: חֵילְךָ֧ וְאוֹצְרוֹתֶ֛יךָ לָבַ֥ז אֶתֵּ֖ן לֹ֣א בִמְחִ֑יר וּבְכָל־חַטֹּאותֶ֖יךָ וּבְכָל־גְּבוּלֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Your wealth and your treasures as plunder I will give, not for price, and for all your sins, and in all your territories.

en.L: Your wealth and your treasures as plunder I will give, not for a price, \q because of all your sins, and in all your territories.
en.B: Your wealth and your treasures I will hand over as plunder, free of charge, \q because of all your sins throughout your territory.
en.R: I will let your enemies take your wealth and your treasures, and I will ask no price for them. \q This is because of all the sins you have committed everywhere in your land.

es.L: Tus riquezas y tus tesoros entregaré al saqueo, sin precio, \q por todos tus pecados, y en todos tus territorios.
es.B: Tus riquezas y tus tesoros los entregaré como botín, sin cobrar nada, \q por todos tus pecados en todo tu territorio.
es.R: Dejaré que tus enemigos se lleven tus riquezas y tus tesoros, y no pediré nada a cambio. \q Esto es por todos los pecados que has cometido en todas partes de tu país.

fr.L: Tes richesses et tes trésors, je les livrerai au pillage, sans prix, \q à cause de tous tes péchés, et dans tout ton territoire.
fr.B: Tes richesses et tes trésors, je les livrerai au pillage, gratuitement, \q à cause de tous tes péchés, dans tout ton territoire.
fr.R: Je laisserai tes ennemis prendre tes richesses et tes trésors, et je ne demanderai rien en échange. \q C’est à cause de tous les péchés que tu as commis partout dans ton pays.

sw.L: Mali yako na hazina zako nitazitoa ziwe mateka, si kwa thamani, \q kwa sababu ya dhambi zako zote, na katika mipaka yako yote.
sw.B: Mali yako na hazina zako nitazitoa ziwe nyara bila malipo, \q kwa sababu ya dhambi zako zote katika nchi yako yote.
sw.R: Nitawaacha adui zako wachukue mali yako na hazina zako, wala sitaomba malipo kwa ajili yake. \q Hii ni kwa sababu ya dhambi zote ulizotenda kila mahali katika nchi yako.

decisions.choice: your: the LORD now speaks to the people of Judah, not to Jeremiah
decisions.reason: Verses 13-14 suddenly address the nation, as the plural "you" at the end of verse 14 shows. It is unclear how they fit after verses 11-12; they may be the LORD's word that Jeremiah must still announce, or a saying placed here from 17:3-4.

decisions.choice: verses 13-14 nearly repeat 17:3-4
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 17:3-4 has almost the same words, with small differences: there the plunder includes the high places, the people are made to serve their enemies, and the fire burns forever.

decisions.choice: not for a price: for nothing, without payment
decisions.reason: The LORD gives away his people's wealth as if it were worth nothing, the way a seller who wants no payment gives goods away (Psalm 44:13; Isaiah 52:3).

decisions.choice: because of all your sins, in all your territories: the sins committed throughout the land
alternatives: your treasures, from all your territories
decisions.reason: The last phrase most likely goes with the sins, as in 17:3, "for sin throughout all your territories". It could also describe the plunder taken from every part of the land.

decisions.choice: I will let your enemies take ... This is because of all the sins
decisions.reason: Readable names the enemies who take the plunder (verse 14) and gives the reason in a separate sentence.

decisions.choice: "tus riquezas" (singular)
decisions.reason: The LORD now speaks to the people of Judah as one, in the singular, as the Hebrew does; in verse 14 "contra ustedes" follows the Hebrew plural.

decisions.choice: the same Swahili in 17:3-4
decisions.reason: Verses 13-14 return almost word for word in 17:3-4 (meaning decision m2); each level keeps the same wording there.

source.text: וְהַֽעֲבַרְתִּי֙ אֶת־אֹ֣יְבֶ֔יךָ בְּאֶ֖רֶץ לֹ֣א יָדָ֑עְתָּ כִּֽי־אֵ֛שׁ קָדְחָ֥ה בְאַפִּ֖י עֲלֵיכֶ֥ם תּוּקָֽד׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And I will make pass your enemies into a land [that] not you have known; for a fire has been kindled in my anger; against you it will burn.

en.L: And I will make [you] pass with your enemies into a land [that] you have not known, \q for a fire has been kindled in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger; against you it will burn.
en.B: I will make you go with your enemies into a land you do not know, \q for a fire has been lit by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger, and it will burn against you.
en.R: I will make you go away with your enemies to a land you have never known. \q My anger is like a fire that has been lit, and it will burn against you.

es.L: Y [te] haré pasar con tus enemigos a una tierra [que] no conoces, \q porque un fuego se ha encendido en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ira; contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} arderá.
es.B: Te haré ir con tus enemigos a una tierra que no conoces, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ira ha encendido un fuego, y arderá contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: Haré que te vayas con tus enemigos a una tierra que nunca has conocido. \q Mi ira es como un fuego que se ha encendido, y arderá contra {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

fr.L: Et je [te] ferai passer avec tes ennemis dans un pays que tu ne connais pas, \q car un feu s’est allumé dans {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colère ; il brûlera contre vous.
fr.B: Je te ferai aller avec tes ennemis dans un pays que tu ne connais pas, \q car un feu s’est allumé dans {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colère, et il brûlera contre vous.
fr.R: Je te ferai partir avec tes ennemis dans un pays que tu n’as jamais connu. \q Ma colère est comme un feu qui s’est allumé, et il va brûler contre vous.

sw.L: Nami nitakupitisha pamoja na adui zako kwenda nchi usiyoijua, \q kwa maana moto umewashwa katika hasira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}; utawaka juu yenu.
sw.B: Nitakufanya uende pamoja na adui zako katika nchi usiyoijua, \q kwa maana moto umewashwa na hasira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, nao utawaka juu yenu.
sw.R: Nitakufanya uende pamoja na adui zako katika nchi ambayo hujawahi kuijua. \q Hasira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ni kama moto uliowashwa, nao utawaka juu yenu.

decisions.choice: I will make you pass: the reading of the Hebrew text here
alternatives: I will make you serve your enemies
decisions.reason: In 17:4 the same saying has "I will make you serve your enemies". The two Hebrew verbs differ by a single letter (r and d look alike in Hebrew script), and some Hebrew manuscripts and early translations read "serve" here too. The Hebrew text of this verse is followed. These statements are made from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: with your enemies: the small word before "your enemies" taken as "with"
alternatives: I will make your enemies pass (with the plunder) into a land you do not know
decisions.reason: The word can mark the object of the verb ("I will make your enemies pass") or mean "with". Read as "with", the people are carried off by their enemies into exile, which suits what follows: a land they do not know.

decisions.choice: a fire has been kindled in my anger: the words of Deuteronomy 32:22
decisions.reason: The Song of Moses says, "For a fire has been kindled in my anger" (Deuteronomy 32:22). Jeremiah 17:4 has the same words, where the fire "will burn forever".

decisions.choice: against you: plural, the whole people
decisions.reason: Here the "you" is plural, which shows that verses 13-14 speak to the nation, not to Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: a fire has been lit by my anger / My anger is like a fire
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly that the fire comes from the LORD's anger.

decisions.choice: juu yenu (plural)
decisions.reason: The last "you" is plural, the whole people (meaning decision m4); Swahili shows it in "yenu".

decisions.choice: "contre vous" after "tu"
decisions.reason: The last pronoun in the Hebrew is plural; French shows the change to "vous", which the English "you" cannot.

source.text: אַתָּ֧ה יָדַ֣עְתָּ יְהוָ֗ה זָכְרֵ֤נִי וּפָקְדֵ֨נִי֙ וְהִנָּ֤קֶם לִי֙ מֵרֹ֣דְפַ֔י אַל־לְאֶ֥רֶךְ אַפְּךָ֖ תִּקָּחֵ֑נִי דַּ֕ע שְׂאֵתִ֥י עָלֶ֖יךָ חֶרְפָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: You, you know, Yahweh; remember me and visit me, and avenge for me from my persecutors; not in [the] length of your anger take me away; know [that] I bear on account of you reproach.

en.L: You know, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}; remember me and visit me, and avenge me on my persecutors; \q in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} slowness to anger do not take me away. \q Know that on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} account I bear reproach.
en.B: You know, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}; remember me and come to my aid, and avenge me on those who hunt me down. \q Do not be so patient with them that I am swept away. \q Know that it is for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sake that I suffer insults.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know what is happening to me. Remember me and help me. Punish the people who keep attacking me. \q Do not be so patient with them that I die before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} act. \q Remember that I am insulted because I serve {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

es.L: Tú lo sabes, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}; acuérdate de mí y visítame, y véngame de mis perseguidores; \q no me lleves en la lentitud de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ira. \q Sabe que por causa {{deity_pronoun:tuya|Tuya}} sufro afrenta.
es.B: Tú lo sabes, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}; acuérdate de mí y ven en mi ayuda, y hazme justicia contra los que me persiguen. \q No seas tan paciente con ellos que yo perezca. \q Sabe que es por {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} causa que sufro insultos.
es.R: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} sabes lo que me está pasando. Acuérdate de mí y ayúdame. Castiga a los que no dejan de atacarme. \q No seas tan paciente con ellos que yo muera antes de que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} actúes. \q Recuerda que me insultan porque {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} sirvo.

fr.L: Toi, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} sais, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ; souviens-toi de moi et visite-moi, et venge-moi de mes persécuteurs ; \q dans la lenteur de {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} colère, ne m’enlève pas. \q Sache que c’est à cause de {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} que je porte l’opprobre.
fr.B: Tu sais, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ; souviens-toi de moi, viens à mon secours, et venge-moi de ceux qui me pourchassent. \q Ne sois pas si patient envers eux que je sois emporté. \q Sache que c’est pour {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} que je supporte les insultes.
fr.R: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} sais ce qui m’arrive. Souviens-toi de moi et aide-moi. Punis les gens qui ne cessent de m’attaquer. \q Ne sois pas si patient avec eux que je meure avant que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} agisses. \q Souviens-toi qu’on m’insulte parce que je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} sers.

sw.L: Wewe unajua, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; unikumbuke na unijilie, unilipizie kisasi kwa wanaonitesa; \q kwa uvumilivu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wa hasira usiniondoe. \q Jua kwamba kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ninastahimili aibu.
sw.B: Wewe unajua, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; unikumbuke na uje kunisaidia, unilipizie kisasi kwa wale wanaoniwinda. \q Usiwavumilie kiasi kwamba mimi niangamie. \q Jua kwamba ni kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} ninavumilia matukano.
sw.R: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} unajua yanayonipata. Unikumbuke na unisaidie. Uwaadhibu watu wanaoendelea kunishambulia. \q Usiwavumilie mno kiasi kwamba nife kabla hujatenda. \q Kumbuka kwamba ninatukanwa kwa sababu ninakutumikia {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}.

decisions.choice: You know, LORD: Jeremiah now speaks directly to God
decisions.reason: The pronoun "you" is written out for emphasis: the LORD knows Jeremiah's case without being told (12:3). From here to verse 18 Jeremiah speaks to God.

decisions.choice: visit me: pay attention to me and act for me
decisions.reason: The verb that meant "appoint" in verse 3 here means to attend to someone and come to their help (Genesis 21:1; Ruth 1:6).

decisions.choice: avenge me: give me justice against those who wrong me
decisions.reason: As in 11:20, Jeremiah does not take revenge himself; he asks God as judge to set things right.

decisions.choice: in your slowness to anger do not take me away: do not be so patient with my enemies that I perish
decisions.reason: Slowness to anger is one of the LORD's great qualities (Exodus 34:6; Numbers 14:18). Jeremiah fears that God's patience toward his persecutors will give them time to kill him. To be "taken away" is to die.

decisions.choice: reproach: insults and scorn
decisions.reason: Jeremiah is mocked because he speaks the LORD's word (20:7-8; Psalm 69:8).

decisions.choice: Do not be so patient with them that I am swept away / that I die before you act
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: what is happening to me ... because I serve you
decisions.reason: Readable says what the LORD knows and why Jeremiah suffers for God's sake.

source.text: נִמְצְא֤וּ דְבָרֶ֨יךָ֙ וָאֹ֣כְלֵ֔ם וַיְהִ֤י דְבָֽרְךָ֙ לִ֔י לְשָׂשׂ֖וֹן וּלְשִׂמְחַ֣ת לְבָבִ֑י כִּֽי־נִקְרָ֤א שִׁמְךָ֙ עָלַ֔י יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י צְבָאֽוֹת׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Were found your words and I ate them, and became your word to me a joy and [the] delight of my heart, for is called your name upon me, Yahweh God of hosts.

en.L: Your words were found, and I ate them, \q and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word became for me joy and the gladness of my heart, \q for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name is called over me, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} God of hosts.
en.B: Your words were found, and I fed on them; \q {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word became a joy to me and gladness to my heart, \q because {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name has been called over me, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies.
en.R: When {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} words were found, I took them in like food. \q They filled me with joy and made my heart glad, \q because I belong to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies.

es.L: Fueron halladas {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} palabras, y yo las comí, \q y {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} palabra fue para mí gozo y alegría de mi corazón, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre es invocado sobre mí, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios de los ejércitos.
es.B: Cuando encontré {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} palabras, me alimenté de ellas; \q {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} palabra fue mi gozo y la alegría de mi corazón, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre ha sido invocado sobre mí, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios de los Ejércitos.
es.R: Cuando encontré {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} palabras, las recibí como alimento. \q Me llenaron de gozo y alegraron mi corazón, \q porque yo {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} pertenezco, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios de los Ejércitos.

fr.L: Tes paroles se sont trouvées, et je les ai mangées, \q et {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} parole est devenue pour moi la joie et l’allégresse de mon cœur, \q car {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom est invoqué sur moi, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu des armées.
fr.B: Tes paroles se sont présentées, et je m’en suis nourri ; \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} parole est devenue ma joie et l’allégresse de mon cœur, \q parce que {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom a été prononcé sur moi, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu des armées.
fr.R: Quand {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} paroles sont arrivées, je les ai prises comme de la nourriture. \q Elles m’ont rempli de joie et ont réjoui mon cœur, \q parce que je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}appartiens, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu des armées.

sw.L: Maneno {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} yalionekana, nami nikayala, \q na neno {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}} likawa kwangu furaha na shangwe ya moyo wangu, \q kwa maana jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}} limeitwa juu yangu, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa majeshi.
sw.B: Maneno {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} yalipatikana, nami nikayala; \q neno {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}} likawa furaha kwangu na shangwe kwa moyo wangu, \q kwa sababu jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}} limeitwa juu yangu, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa majeshi.
sw.R: Maneno {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} yalipopatikana, niliyapokea kama chakula. \q Yalinijaza furaha na kuufurahisha moyo wangu, \q kwa sababu mimi ni mali {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa majeshi.

decisions.choice: I ate them: I took your words in fully and made them my own
decisions.reason: Eating God's words is a picture of receiving them gladly and wholly (Ezekiel 2:8-3:3). The LORD had put his words in Jeremiah's mouth (1:9).

decisions.choice: your words were found: possibly the book of the law found in the temple
decisions.reason: In Josiah's reign, when Jeremiah's work began (1:2), the book of the law was found in the temple (2 Kings 22:8, 13), and the same verb is used there. The words may simply mean that God's message came to Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: your name is called over me: I belong to you
decisions.reason: To have someone's name called over a person or a thing marks it as belonging to that one (7:10-11; 14:9; Deuteronomy 28:10). Jeremiah is the LORD's own prophet.

decisions.choice: a joy and the delight of my heart
decisions.reason: The two words for joy belong to the sounds of weddings and feasts (7:34; 16:9). Jeremiah had no part in such joy (verse 17), but God's word gave him gladness.

decisions.choice: I fed on them
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of eating with a phrase that suggests taking nourishment.

decisions.choice: I belong to you
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the idiom (meaning decision m3) and adds "like food" to the picture of eating.

decisions.choice: LORD God of hosts (Literal) / LORD God of Armies (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The title follows the wording of "the LORD of hosts" set for Isaiah and Jeremiah; addressed directly, it has no "O".

decisions.choice: BWANA Mungu wa majeshi
decisions.reason: "Mungu wa majeshi" at every level, as "BWANA wa majeshi" is, where the English Balanced and Readable say "of Armies".

source.text: לֹֽא־יָשַׁ֥בְתִּי בְסוֹד־מְשַׂחֲקִ֖ים וָֽאֶעְלֹ֑ז מִפְּנֵ֤י יָֽדְךָ֙ בָּדָ֣ד יָשַׁ֔בְתִּי כִּֽי־זַ֖עַם מִלֵּאתָֽנִי׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Not I sat in [the] company of merrymakers and I exulted; because of your hand alone I sat, for [with] indignation you filled me.

en.L: I did not sit in the company of merrymakers and rejoice; \q because of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand I sat alone, \q for with indignation {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} had filled me.
en.B: I never sat in the circle of revelers or celebrated with them; \q with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand on me I sat by myself, \q because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} had filled me with indignation.
en.R: I did not sit with people who laugh and have a good time, or join in their fun. \q I sat by myself because {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand was on me, \q and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} had filled me with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger against the people.

es.L: No me senté en la reunión de los que se divierten ni me regocijé; \q a causa de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} mano me senté solo, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} me llenaste de indignación.
es.B: Nunca me senté en el círculo de los que se divierten ni celebré con ellos; \q con {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} mano sobre mí me senté aparte, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} me habías llenado de indignación.
es.R: No me senté con la gente que ríe y lo pasa bien, ni me uní a su diversión. \q Me senté solo porque {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} mano estaba sobre mí, \q y {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} me habías llenado de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} enojo contra el pueblo.

fr.L: Je ne me suis pas assis dans le cercle des rieurs et je ne me suis pas réjoui ; \q à cause de {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} main, je me suis assis seul, \q car {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} m’avais rempli d’indignation.
fr.B: Je ne me suis jamais assis dans le cercle des fêtards ni n’ai fait la fête avec eux ; \q sous {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} main, je me suis assis à l’écart, \q parce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} m’avais rempli d’indignation.
fr.R: Je ne me suis pas assis avec les gens qui rient et s’amusent, et je n’ai pas pris part à leurs fêtes. \q Je suis resté seul parce que {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} main était sur moi, \q et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} m’avais rempli de {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} colère contre le peuple.

sw.L: Sikuketi katika kundi la wenye kufanya sherehe nikashangilia; \q kwa sababu ya mkono {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} niliketi peke yangu, \q kwa maana ulikuwa umenijaza ghadhabu.
sw.B: Sikuketi kamwe katika mzunguko wa wanaofanya karamu wala kusherehekea pamoja nao; \q mkono {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} ukiwa juu yangu niliketi peke yangu, \q kwa sababu ulikuwa umenijaza ghadhabu.
sw.R: Sikuketi pamoja na watu wanaocheka na kujifurahisha, wala sikujiunga na michezo yao. \q Niliketi peke yangu kwa sababu mkono {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} ulikuwa juu yangu, \q nawe ulikuwa umenijaza hasira {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} dhidi ya watu.

decisions.choice: the company of merrymakers: a circle of people enjoying themselves
decisions.reason: The word for "company" means a close circle of friends who sit and talk together. The merrymakers are people laughing and celebrating, not necessarily wicked; Jeremiah could not share their light-hearted life (16:8-9).

decisions.choice: because of your hand: because of the LORD's power laid on me as a prophet
decisions.reason: The LORD's hand is his power taking hold of a prophet and compelling him (Isaiah 8:11; Ezekiel 1:3; 3:14).

decisions.choice: indignation: the LORD's anger against his people
decisions.reason: Jeremiah is filled with God's own indignation at the people's sin, which he must announce (6:11, "I am full of the wrath of the LORD"). It sets him apart from everyone around him.

decisions.choice: with your hand on me / your hand was on me
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say how the LORD's hand caused Jeremiah to sit alone (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: your anger against the people
decisions.reason: Readable says whose indignation fills Jeremiah and against whom it is directed (meaning decision m3).

source.text: לָ֣מָּה הָיָ֤ה כְאֵבִי֙ נֶ֔צַח וּמַכָּתִ֖י אֲנוּשָׁ֑ה֙ מֵֽאֲנָה֙ הֵֽרָפֵ֔א הָי֨וֹ תִֽהְיֶ֥ה לִי֙ כְּמ֣וֹ אַכְזָ֔ב מַ֖יִם לֹ֥א נֶאֱמָֽנוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Why has been my pain perpetual and my wound incurable, it refuses to be healed? Surely you will be to me like a deceitful [brook], waters [that] not are reliable.

en.L: Why has my pain been unending, and my wound incurable? \q It refuses to be healed. \q Will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} indeed be to me like a deceptive [brook], \q waters [that] are not reliable?
en.B: Why is my pain endless and my wound beyond cure? \q It will not heal. \q Will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} truly be to me like a stream that deceives, \q like waters that cannot be trusted?
en.R: Why does my pain never stop? Why is my wound so bad? \q It will not heal. \q Will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} be like a stream that dries up \q and leaves me with no water?

es.L: ¿Por qué ha sido perpetuo mi dolor, y mi herida incurable? \q No admite curación. \q ¿Serás {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} para mí como [arroyo] engañoso, \q aguas en que no se puede confiar?
es.B: ¿Por qué mi dolor no tiene fin y mi herida no tiene cura? \q No quiere sanar. \q ¿Serás de veras {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} para mí como un arroyo que engaña, \q como aguas en las que no se puede confiar?
es.R: ¿Por qué mi dolor nunca se acaba? ¿Por qué es tan grave mi herida? \q No sana. \q ¿Serás {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} como un arroyo que se seca \q y me deja sin agua?

fr.L: Pourquoi ma douleur est-elle perpétuelle, et ma plaie incurable ? \q Elle refuse de guérir. \q Serais-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} vraiment pour moi comme un [torrent] trompeur, \q des eaux sur lesquelles on ne peut compter ?
fr.B: Pourquoi ma douleur est-elle sans fin et ma blessure sans remède ? \q Elle ne veut pas guérir. \q Serais-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} vraiment pour moi comme un ruisseau qui trompe, \q comme des eaux auxquelles on ne peut se fier ?
fr.R: Pourquoi ma douleur ne s’arrête-t-elle jamais ? Pourquoi ma blessure est-elle si grave ? \q Elle ne guérit pas. \q Seras-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} comme un ruisseau qui s’assèche \q et qui me laisse sans eau ?

sw.L: Mbona maumivu yangu yamekuwa ya daima, na jeraha langu lisiloponyeka? \q Linakataa kuponywa. \q Je, kweli {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} utakuwa kwangu kama [kijito] cha udanganyifu, \q maji yasiyoaminika?
sw.B: Mbona maumivu yangu hayana mwisho na jeraha langu halitibiki? \q Halitaki kupona. \q Je, kweli {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} utakuwa kwangu kama kijito kinachodanganya, \q kama maji yasiyoweza kutegemewa?
sw.R: Kwa nini maumivu yangu hayakomi? Kwa nini jeraha langu ni baya hivi? \q Halitaki kupona. \q Je, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} utakuwa kama kijito kinachokauka \q na kuniacha bila maji?

decisions.choice: a deceptive brook: a stream bed that runs dry in summer
decisions.reason: Many streams in the land flow only in the rainy season. A traveler who counts on them in the dry months finds nothing (Job 6:15-20). In 2:13 the LORD called himself "the fountain of living waters"; now Jeremiah fears that God has become like a stream that fails.

decisions.choice: will you indeed be to me: a bitter question, or a statement
alternatives: You have surely become to me like a deceptive brook
decisions.reason: The Hebrew doubles the verb for emphasis. It can be read as a question ("Will you really be ...?") or as a statement ("You have surely become ..."). Either way it is Jeremiah's boldest complaint, and the LORD answers it in verse 19.

decisions.choice: my pain ... my wound incurable: Jeremiah's own suffering
decisions.reason: The words that described the people's wound in 10:19 and 14:17 are now used of the prophet's own pain, both inward grief and the hurt done him by his enemies.

decisions.choice: a stream that dries up and leaves me with no water
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (meaning decision m1).

source.text: לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אִם־תָּשׁ֤וּב וַאֲשִֽׁיבְךָ֙ לְפָנַ֣י תַּֽעֲמֹ֔ד וְאִם־תּוֹצִ֥יא יָקָ֛ר מִזּוֹלֵ֖ל כְּפִ֣י תִֽהְיֶ֑ה יָשֻׁ֤בוּ הֵ֨מָּה֙ אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְאַתָּ֖ה לֹֽא־תָשׁ֥וּב אֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore thus says Yahweh: If you return, then I will bring you back; before me you will stand; and if you bring out [the] precious from [the] worthless, like my mouth you will be; they will return to you, and you, not you will return to them.

en.L: Therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: If you return, I will bring you back; before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} you will stand. \q And if you bring out what is precious from what is worthless, you will be as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mouth. \q They will return to you, \q but you, you will not return to them.
