en.B: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: If you turn back, I will take you back, and you will stand before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q If you bring out what is precious and not what is worthless, you will be as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mouth. \q They may turn to you, \q but you are not to turn to them.
en.R: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: If you come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I will take you back, and you will serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} again. \q If you speak words that are worth something and not worthless words, you will speak for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q The people must come over to your side; \q you must not go over to theirs.

es.L: Por tanto, así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Si vuelves, yo te haré volver; delante de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} estarás. \q Y si sacas lo precioso de lo vil, serás como {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} boca. \q Ellos se volverán a ti, \q pero tú no te volverás a ellos.
es.B: Por eso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: Si vuelves, yo te haré volver, y estarás delante de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. \q Si pronuncias lo precioso y no lo vil, serás como {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} boca. \q Que ellos se vuelvan a ti, \q pero tú no te vuelvas a ellos.
es.R: Por eso, esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Si regresas a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, te recibiré otra vez, y volverás a servir{{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q Si dices palabras que valen algo y no palabras vacías, hablarás en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre. \q La gente tiene que pasarse a tu lado; \q tú no debes pasarte al de ellos.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Si tu reviens, je te ferai revenir ; devant {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} tu te tiendras. \q Et si tu sépares ce qui est précieux de ce qui est vil, tu seras comme {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} bouche. \q C’est eux qui reviendront vers toi, \q mais toi, tu ne reviendras pas vers eux.
fr.B: C’est pourquoi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Si tu reviens, je te reprendrai, et tu te tiendras devant {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. \q Si tu fais sortir ce qui est précieux et non ce qui est vil, tu seras comme {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} bouche. \q Qu’ils reviennent vers toi, \q mais toi, ne reviens pas vers eux.
fr.R: Alors voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Si tu reviens vers {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je te reprendrai, et tu {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} serviras de nouveau. \q Si tu dis des paroles qui ont de la valeur et non des paroles sans valeur, tu parleras de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} part. \q C’est le peuple qui doit venir de ton côté ; \q toi, tu ne dois pas passer du sien.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: Ukirudi, nitakurudisha; utasimama mbele {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. \q Na ukitoa kilicho cha thamani kutoka kisichofaa, utakuwa kama kinywa {{deity_pronoun:changu|Changu}}. \q Wao watakurudia wewe, \q lakini wewe hutawarudia wao.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: Ukirudi, nitakupokea tena, nawe utasimama mbele {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. \q Ukitamka yaliyo ya thamani wala si yasiyofaa, utakuwa kama kinywa {{deity_pronoun:changu|Changu}}. \q Wao na wakugeukie wewe, \q lakini wewe usiwageukie wao.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: Ukinirudia, nitakupokea tena, nawe utanitumikia tena. \q Ukisema maneno yenye thamani wala si maneno yasiyofaa kitu, utasema kwa niaba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. \q Watu ndio wanaopaswa kuja upande wako; \q wewe usiende upande wao.

decisions.choice: return ... bring you back ... they will return ... you will not return: a play on one verb
decisions.reason: The same verb, "turn" or "return", is used four times. Jeremiah must turn back from his bitter words of verse 18; then the LORD will restore him. The people must turn to the prophet, not the prophet to the people.

decisions.choice: stand before me: serve me as my prophet
decisions.reason: Those who stand before a king are his servants (1 Kings 10:8); Elijah spoke of "the LORD, before whom I stand" (1 Kings 17:1). Moses and Samuel stood before the LORD to plead (verse 1); Jeremiah will again stand before him.

decisions.choice: bring out what is precious from what is worthless: speak worthy words, not worthless ones
alternatives: separate the precious from the worthless
decisions.reason: The words may mean to separate the precious from the worthless, as a refiner separates metal (6:27-30), or to speak what is precious rather than what is worthless. Either way Jeremiah must speak only what is true and worthy, and not complaints like those of verse 18.

decisions.choice: you will be as my mouth: you will be my spokesman
decisions.reason: The LORD told Moses that Aaron would be his mouth and Moses would be like God to him (Exodus 4:15-16). A prophet speaks for God; the LORD had put his words in Jeremiah's mouth (1:9).

decisions.choice: They may turn to you, but you are not to turn to them / The people must come over to your side
alternatives: They will turn to you, but you will not turn to them
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verbs can state what will happen or what should happen; Balanced and Readable express the LORD's command, and Readable explains the picture of turning.

decisions.choice: serve me again ... speak for me
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "stand before me" and "be as my mouth" (meaning decisions m2 and m4).

decisions.choice: "vuelves ... te haré volver ... se volverán ... no te volverás"
decisions.reason: Shuv four times, kept as "volver" every time at Literal and Balanced so the play on the one verb stays; Readable says it plainly, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Ukirudi, nitakurudisha ... watakurudia ... hutawarudia (Literal)
decisions.reason: One verb, shuv, runs through the verse (meaning decision m1); Literal keeps "-rudi" each time, and Balanced and Readable keep it where the sense allows.

decisions.choice: "revenir" for every *shuv* in the verse
decisions.reason: The Hebrew plays on one verb four times; "revenir", the settled word for *shuv*, keeps the play at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: וּנְתַתִּ֜יךָ לָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֗ה לְחוֹמַ֤ת נְחֹ֨שֶׁת֙ בְּצוּרָ֔ה וְנִלְחֲמ֥וּ אֵלֶ֖יךָ וְלֹא־י֣וּכְלוּ לָ֑ךְ כִּֽי־אִתְּךָ֥ אֲנִ֛י לְהוֹשִֽׁיעֲךָ֥ וּלְהַצִּילֶ֖ךָ נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will make you to the people the this into a wall of bronze fortified; and they will fight against you, and not they will prevail over you, for with you I [am] to save you and to deliver you, declares Yahweh.

en.L: And I will make you to this people into a wall of bronze, fortified; \q and they will fight against you, but they will not prevail against you, \q for with you I [am] to save you and to deliver you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: I will make you a fortified wall of bronze facing this people; \q they will make war on you, but they will not overcome you, \q for I am with you to save you and to rescue you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: I will make you like a strong wall of bronze that this people cannot break through. \q They will fight against you, but they will not defeat you. \q I am with you, and I will save you and keep you safe, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y te pondré para este pueblo por muro de bronce fortificado; \q y pelearán contra ti, pero no prevalecerán contra ti, \q porque contigo [estoy] yo para salvarte y para librarte, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Te pondré frente a este pueblo como un muro fortificado de bronce; \q te harán la guerra, pero no te vencerán, \q porque yo estoy contigo para salvarte y para rescatarte, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Haré de ti un muro fuerte de bronce que este pueblo no podrá atravesar. \q Pelearán contra ti, pero no te derrotarán. \q Yo estoy contigo, y te salvaré y te protegeré, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et je ferai de toi pour ce peuple une muraille de bronze fortifiée ; \q et ils combattront contre toi, mais ils ne l’emporteront pas sur toi, \q car avec toi je [suis] pour te sauver et pour te délivrer, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Je ferai de toi, face à ce peuple, une muraille de bronze fortifiée ; \q ils te feront la guerre, mais ils ne te vaincront pas, \q car je suis avec toi pour te sauver et te délivrer, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Je ferai de toi comme une solide muraille de bronze que ce peuple ne pourra pas percer. \q Ils te combattront, mais ils ne te vaincront pas. \q Je suis avec toi, et je te sauverai et te protégerai, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Nami nitakufanya kwa watu hawa kuwa ukuta wa shaba wenye ngome; \q nao watapigana nawe, lakini hawatakushinda, \q kwa maana pamoja nawe mimi [niko] kukuokoa na kukuponya, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Nitakufanya kuwa ukuta wa shaba wenye ngome mbele ya watu hawa; \q watapigana nawe, lakini hawatakushinda, \q kwa maana niko pamoja nawe ili nikuokoe na kukuponya, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Nitakufanya kuwa kama ukuta imara wa shaba ambao watu hawa hawawezi kuupenya. \q Watapigana nawe, lakini hawatakushinda. \q Niko pamoja nawe, nami nitakuokoa na kukulinda salama, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

decisions.choice: a fortified wall of bronze ... they will not prevail: the LORD renews the promise he gave at Jeremiah's call
decisions.reason: Verses 20-21 repeat the promise of 1:18-19 almost word for word: "walls of bronze", "they will fight against you, but they will not prevail", "I am with you to deliver you". The LORD answers the prophet's despair by restating the promise first made to him.

decisions.choice: to save you and to deliver you
decisions.reason: The two verbs mean to rescue from danger and to snatch out of an enemy's hand. Verse 21 takes up the second verb.

decisions.choice: the wording of 1:18-19 at each level
decisions.reason: Where the Hebrew repeats 1:18-19, each level repeats its own wording of those verses, so the reader can see the promise renewed.

decisions.choice: the wording of 1:18-19 at each level
decisions.reason: The promise of Jeremiah's call is renewed in its own words, so each level keeps its wording of 1:18-19.

decisions.choice: the Swahili of 1:18-19 at each level
decisions.reason: The LORD renews the promise of Jeremiah's call (meaning decision m1), and each level keeps the wording it has in 1:18-19.

decisions.choice: the wording of 1:18-19 at each level
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the promise of Jeremiah's call, so each French level repeats its own wording there.

records.literal_gloss: And I will deliver you from [the] hand of [the] wicked, and I will redeem you from [the] palm of [the] ruthless.

en.L: And I will deliver you from the hand of the wicked, \q and I will redeem you from the palm of the ruthless.
en.B: I will rescue you from the power of the wicked \q and ransom you from the grip of the ruthless.
en.R: I will rescue you from wicked people \q and set you free from the power of cruel people.

es.L: Y te libraré de la mano de los malvados, \q y te redimiré de la palma de los violentos.
es.B: Te rescataré del poder de los malvados \q y te liberaré de las garras de los violentos.
es.R: Te rescataré de la gente malvada \q y te libraré del poder de la gente cruel.

fr.L: Et je te délivrerai de la main des méchants, \q et je te rachèterai de la paume des violents.
fr.B: Je te délivrerai du pouvoir des méchants \q et je te rachèterai de la poigne des tyrans.
fr.R: Je te sauverai des gens méchants \q et je te libérerai du pouvoir des gens cruels.

sw.L: Nami nitakuponya kutoka mkononi mwa waovu, \q nami nitakukomboa kutoka kiganjani mwa wakatili.
sw.B: Nitakuokoa kutoka katika nguvu za waovu \q na kukukomboa kutoka katika makucha ya wakatili.
sw.R: Nitakuokoa kutoka kwa watu waovu \q na kukuweka huru kutoka katika uwezo wa watu wakatili.

decisions.choice: redeem you: set you free by paying the price
decisions.reason: The verb means to ransom or buy free, as the LORD redeemed Israel from slavery in Egypt (Deuteronomy 7:8; 13:6). The LORD himself will pay what it takes to free his prophet.

decisions.choice: the ruthless: violent, terrifying oppressors
decisions.reason: The word describes those who use force without mercy (Isaiah 29:20; Psalm 54:5). In Jeremiah's case they are the powerful men of Judah who persecute him (verse 15).

decisions.choice: the hand ... the palm: the power and grip of an enemy
decisions.reason: The hand and the palm stand for power and control; to be in someone's hand is to be in their power.

decisions.choice: the power of the wicked ... the grip of the ruthless
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "hand" and "palm" (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: nitakukomboa
decisions.reason: "Kukomboa", to redeem, at Literal and Balanced as the terms note sets it; Readable says "set you free".
